memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Whoever touches a human corpse will be unclean for seven days. They must purify themselves with the water on the third day and on the seventh day; then they will be clean. But if they do not purify themselves on the third and seventh days, they will not be clean. If they fail to purify themselves after touching a human corpse, they defile the Lord's tabernacle. They must be cut off from Israel." — Num 19:11-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This whole ceremony centred on contact with death. Touching a corpse made a person ceremonially unclean, and they needed the water of cleansing to be restored. This was not because death was sinful in itself, but because death is the great enemy, the wound sin brought into God's good world. Contact with it was a reminder that something had gone deeply wrong.

Death is the one reality none of us can avoid, and it touches all of us. The people of Israel were taught, through these laws, that death is not natural or acceptable in God's presence, but an intruder. Every encounter with it required cleansing before one could draw near to a holy, living God. Death and the presence of the living God did not belong together.

We live in a world that often tries to hide from death, keeping it at arm's length. But Scripture faces it honestly. Death is real, it is serious, and by ourselves we have no power over it. These laws gently forced God's people to reckon with mortality rather than ignore it.

Yet here is the glory of the gospel: Jesus entered death itself and conquered it. Where the old ceremony could only cleanse those who touched death, Christ went into death and came out victorious, breaking its power forever. He touched our mortality — the ultimate defilement — and instead of being overcome, He overcame. Because He lives, death is no longer the final word for those who trust Him. The One who swallowed up death in victory has turned our greatest enemy into a defeated foe. In Him, we need not fear the grave.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you face the reality of death honestly, or try to hide from it?
2. Why did contact with death require cleansing before approaching God?
3. How does Christ's victory over death change the way you face it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Jesus entered death and conquered it forever. Help me to face my mortality honestly, yet without fear, because Christ has won the victory. Because He lives, the grave is not my final word. Amen.
